headline_marked: [[Vinicius Jr. scores twice as Brazil]] beats Scotland 3-0, advances to World Cup knockouts
headline: Vinicius Jr. scores twice as Brazil beats Scotland 3-0, advances to World Cup knockouts
summary: Vinicius Junior netted two goals, and Matheus Cunha added another, securing Brazil's dominant 3-0 victory over Scotland. This win propelled them to the top of Group C and into the World Cup's second round.
details: Vinicius Junior scored two goals, leading Brazil to a dominant 3-0 victory over Scotland and securing their spot as Group C winners in the World Cup's second round. The Real Madrid forward opened the scoring in the seventh minute after a Scottish defensive error.

He then added his second goal with a header in first-half stoppage time, extending Brazil's lead. Matheus Cunha sealed the comfortable win with a third goal on the hour mark, ensuring Brazil's progression.

The match also marked the return of star player Neymar after a long absence, further bolstering the Brazilian squad. This victory, combined with Morocco's 4-2 win over Haiti, sets Brazil on course for Houston.

Brazil will now face either the Netherlands, Japan, or Sweden in their next match on Monday. Scotland, after a timid and error-prone display, must now rely on other results to advance as one of the best third-placed teams.

headline_marked: [[Morocco secure last 32 spot]] with 4-2 comeback win over Haiti in World Cup thriller
headline: Morocco secure last 32 spot with 4-2 comeback win over Haiti in World Cup thriller
summary: Morocco twice overcame conceding to Haiti to win 4-2, but missed out on top spot in Group C to Brazil. Haiti scored their first World Cup goals in 52 years.
details: Morocco defeated Haiti 4-2 in a thrilling World Cup match in Atlanta, securing their place in the last 32. They twice came from behind, with Haiti scoring their first World Cup goals in 52 years.

Haiti initially took the lead twice, first through a Yassine Bounou own goal and then with a stunning strike from Wilson Isidor. Achraf Hakimi and Ismael Saibari equalized for Morocco before halftime.

Soufiane Rahimi's deflected effort gave Morocco the lead, and Gessime Yassine rounded off the scoring to make it 4-2. Despite the victory, Morocco finished second in Group C, behind Brazil on goal difference.

Morocco will now proceed to Monterrey for their last 32 fixture, likely facing either the Netherlands or Japan. Haiti, though eliminated without points, showcased a proud performance at their first World Cup since 1974.
